claims.text: Abstraction removes unnecessary detail from a system so that only the details that matter for the purpose remain, and what counts as unnecessary is decided by what the model is for.

claims.text: Abstraction keeps a model small enough to understand, build and check, because leaving out what does not matter leaves only what the purpose needs.

claims.text: Decomposition breaks a problem into smaller sub-problems, each solvable on its own, whose solutions combine to solve the whole problem.

claims.text: A sub-problem that does one clear job becomes a program module - a procedure or a function - so decomposition leads to modules that can be written, tested and reused separately.
